customer: Agreement to These Terms

POTENT LOGISTICS LLC (DOT# 9166689, 2089 Christian Cir SE, Conyers, GA 30013) ("POTENT," "we," "us") provides delivery, freight, junk removal, cleanout and related hauling services in Georgia and nearby areas. By booking a job, accepting a quote, paying a deposit or invoice, or letting us start work, you ("Customer," "you") agree to these Terms, our Privacy Policy, and any written quote or rate confirmation for your job (together, the "Agreement"). If you are booking for a business, you confirm you have authority to bind it. If you do not agree, do not book.
Electronic Agreement and Signature

You agree that clicking a box, typing your name, replying "yes" to a written quote, paying, or letting us begin work is a legally binding electronic signature under the federal E-SIGN Act and Georgia's Uniform Electronic Transactions Act. We keep a record of the version you accepted, the time, and the device and network address used, so the exact terms that applied to your job can be shown later.
Our Services

Delivery and freight: pickup and delivery of items you describe, in a 16-foot box truck, to the addresses on your booking. Junk removal and cleanouts: loading, hauling and lawful disposal of items you identify. We are a hauler. We are not a moving company, do not pack, crate or disassemble furniture unless a quote says so, and do not handle hazardous, regulated or illegal items. Services are provided in the order and time windows we confirm. Time windows are estimates, not guarantees, unless confirmed in writing.
Quotes and Pricing

A quote is based on what you tell us: addresses, distance, item list and photos, access, load size and weight. Distance is measured by road from our base, including the trip to you and the return, using mapping data. A quote is valid for the date and time window it states. Prices do not include items or conditions you did not tell us about. Payment methods accepted: card and cash. We do not accept checks. Paying in cash may earn a discount on the base job price where we advertise one; the discount does not apply to disposal weight charges, heavy-item fees or third-party fees.
Weight, Heavy Items and Disposal Charges

Landfills and transfer stations charge us by weight. You must tell us about heavy items (for example safes, pianos, hot tubs, exercise equipment, appliances, concrete, brick, dirt, tile, roofing and similar material) and give an accurate weight or your best honest estimate. Heavy items and loose heavy material are priced by weight in addition to the load price. Our truck carries a maximum of 4,300 pounds of junk per trip. If the load is heavier or bigger than the quote, we will tell you, and we may need extra trips, a second truck, or a roll-off container, each at the price we quote you before we proceed. Special-disposal items (mattresses, tires, refrigerants, electronics, paint, propane tanks and similar) carry the per-item fee on our price list.
Scope Differences and Price Changes On Site

If the job on site is materially different from what was described (more items, heavier items, different access, stairs, longer carry, different address, or items we cannot take), our driver will pause and contact our office with photos. We will give you a revised price and wait for your approval before continuing. Work then proceeds only on your approval. If you decline the revised price, we will stop, you will owe the minimum charge in the price list plus any time, travel and disposal already incurred, and we will not remove anything we have not been paid to remove.
Items We Cannot Accept

We do not transport or dispose of hazardous waste, chemicals, fuel, solvents, asbestos, biohazards, medical waste, ammunition, explosives, firearms, controlled substances, human or animal remains, or anything illegal, stolen or subject to a lien or legal hold. You confirm that you own the items or are authorized to have them moved or discarded, and that nothing in the load is prohibited. We may refuse any item for safety, legal or weight reasons and may charge for time already spent.
Access, Site Conditions and Your Responsibilities

You must provide safe, legal access to the pickup and drop-off locations, working elevators or loading areas when applicable, and a person authorized to release or accept the items. Please secure pets, remove valuables and personal papers, and tell us about fragile, valuable or sentimental items before we begin. We are not responsible for items that are not disclosed, for pre-existing damage to floors, walls, doors or property, or for hidden conditions such as weak flooring or unmarked utilities, except where caused by our negligence.
Photos and Documentation

Our drivers photograph the job at pickup, during loading, at delivery or disposal, and at completion, and may record a signed bill of lading or proof of delivery. Photos are timestamped and may include your property and the items. We keep them as job records and for claims, disputes and quality control. Do not remove or hide items before we photograph them.
Scheduling, Delays and Cancellation

Cancellation policy: 48 or more hours before the arranged time, cancellation is free with a full refund or credit. 24 to 48 hours before, a 50% cancellation fee applies. Under 24 hours, the $100 dispatch fee is retained and the balance refunded. Same-day and urgent bookings are final and non-refundable once confirmed. If we cannot start because access is unavailable, no one is present, or the job is not as described, we may charge a trip charge. Time windows are estimates. We are not liable for delays caused by weather, traffic, road closures, breakdown, accident or events outside our reasonable control; we will keep you informed and reschedule at no extra charge.
Waiting Time and Extra Labor
Time on site begins when the truck arrives. Where a price list provides included time, additional time and extra helpers are billed at the posted hourly rate, in increments we state.
Payment

Payment is due when the job is completed unless we agreed otherwise in writing. Approved business accounts may be on invoice terms of up to Net 7 days. Commercial interest: past-due balances on commercial accounts accrue a finance charge of 1.5% per month (18% per year), or the maximum allowed by law if lower. Consumer balances: past-due balances of non-commercial customers accrue interest only at the rate Georgia law allows. Collection costs and attorneys' fees: if a balance is collected through an attorney after it is due, you agree to pay attorneys' fees to the extent allowed by O.C.G.A. section 13-1-11 (15% of the first $500 of principal and interest owed and 10% of the rest), but only after we send you the written 10-day notice that statute requires and you do not pay the principal and interest within that time. Reasonable collection costs are also owed to the extent Georgia law allows. A chargeback or payment reversal for a job we completed as agreed may be disputed with the documentation described above. Returned or failed payments may carry a fee permitted by law.
Taxes and Fees

Prices exclude any sales or use tax, tolls, permits, parking, or third-party container, landfill or disposal charges that apply to your job, which will be shown on your quote or invoice when known. Card payments may be processed by Stripe or another processor; their terms apply to the payment.
Insurance

POTENT maintains commercial auto liability and motor-truck cargo insurance. Cargo coverage applies to freight we accept in our truck while in our care, subject to its terms, exclusions and limits. Insurance does not cover items you did not disclose, pre-existing damage, items of extraordinary value, or items excluded by the policy. To make a claim, follow the Claims section.
Limits on Our Liability for Loss or Damage

For delivery and freight, unless you declare a higher value in writing before pickup and we agree in writing, our liability for loss of or damage to an item is limited to the lesser of (a) the item's actual value or repair cost, (b) $0.60 per pound per article, or (c) $100,000 per shipment. You may request a higher released value for an additional charge before pickup. For junk removal and cleanouts, items you have asked us to remove and dispose of have no recoverable value to you. We are not responsible for items that are discarded in accordance with your instructions.
Claims

Report any damage, loss or complaint to potentlogistics@pm.me or (770) 648-4228 in writing within 48 hours of delivery for freight, or 7 days of completion for other services, with photos and a description. Claims reported later may be declined to the extent the delay prejudiced our ability to investigate. We will acknowledge a claim within two business days and respond after our review.
Disclaimer

Except as stated in this Agreement, services are provided "as is" and "as available." To the extent permitted by law, we disclaim all other warranties, express or implied, including fitness for a particular purpose. Nothing in this Agreement limits rights you have under law that cannot be waived.
Limitation of Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by law, POTENT's total liability arising out of a job, whether in contract, tort (including negligence) or otherwise, is limited to the amount you paid for that job, subject to the cargo limits above. We are not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, including lost profits, lost business, or emotional distress. This section does not limit liability that cannot be limited under applicable law, such as liability for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bodily injury or death caused by our negligence.
Indemnity

You agree to defend and indemnify POTENT against claims, losses and reasonable costs from third parties arising out of inaccurate information you gave us, items you were not entitled to give us, prohibited or undisclosed hazardous items, or your breach of this Agreement. This does not apply to the extent a claim is caused by POTENT's negligence or willful misconduct.
Independent Contractors and Subcontractors

We may use qualified drivers, helpers, vendors, container companies and disposal facilities to perform your job. We remain responsible to you for the service we sell you. Our drivers are not authorized to change prices, waive terms or accept payment except as our office directs.
Disputes: Informal Resolution First
Before filing a claim, you agree to contact us at potentlogistics@pm.me and give us 30 days to resolve the issue. Most issues are resolved this way.
Binding Individual Arbitration

If we cannot resolve a dispute informally, it will be decided by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its rules for the type of dispute, in Rockdale County, Georgia or by video, in individual proceedings. The Federal Arbitration Act governs this section. Either party may bring an individual claim in small-claims court instead. You may opt out of arbitration by emailing potentlogistics@pm.me within 30 days of first accepting these Terms; opting out does not affect any other term. A court, not the arbitrator, decides whether the class waiver is enforceable, and if it is found unenforceable as to a claim, that claim will proceed in court and not in arbitration.
No Class Actions
To the extent allowed by law, disputes will be brought only in the claimant's individual capacity and not as a plaintiff or class member in any class, collective or representative action.
Governing Law and Venue

Georgia law governs this Agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules, except that the Federal Arbitration Act applies to arbitration and federal transportation law applies where it governs interstate carriage. For any dispute that proceeds in court, the state and federal courts for Rockdale County, Georgia have exclusive jurisdiction and you consent to them.
Privacy, Texts and Calls

We use your information as described in our Privacy Policy. By giving us your mobile number you agree we may send job-related text messages and calls (confirmations, arrival and tracking updates, receipts, claims follow-up). Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to end texts; this does not stop essential calls about a job in progress. Marketing messages are sent only if you separately agree.
Changes, Entire Agreement, Severability

We may update these Terms. The version in force when you booked, shown on your confirmation, governs your job. If a provision is unenforceable, the rest remains in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver. This Agreement, with your written quote or rate confirmation, is the entire agreement for the job; a signed quote controls over these Terms if they conflict.
Contact

carrier: Parties, Purpose and Order of Documents

This Dispatch / Carrier Agreement is between POTENT LOGISTICS LLC (DOT# 9166689, EIN 42-2446741, 2089 Christian Cir SE, Conyers, GA 30013) ("POTENT" or "Carrier") and the dispatcher, broker, shipper or company that completes this onboarding ("Dispatch Partner"). It sets the standing terms for every load POTENT accepts from Dispatch Partner. Each load is confirmed by its own written rate confirmation. If the two conflict, the rate confirmation controls for that load only.
Term and Termination

This Agreement begins when Dispatch Partner accepts it and continues until ended. Either party may end it at any time on written notice, and immediately for the other's material breach, loss of required authority or insurance, or fraud. Ending the Agreement does not cancel a load already accepted or any amount already owed.
Verification of Dispatch Partner

Before accepting freight, POTENT may verify identity and authority, including USDOT and MC numbers with FMCSA, the surety bond or trust fund required of brokers, business registration, and references. Dispatch Partner confirms the information it gives is true and will notify POTENT promptly of changes. Dispatchers acting without their own authority must say so and may only offer loads they are legally authorized to offer.
Carrier's Operating Authority and Compliance

POTENT represents that it holds the operating authority and registrations required for the services it performs and will comply with applicable federal, state and local transportation, safety and employment law.
Broker and Shipper Representations

Dispatch Partner represents that it has the right to tender each load, that load descriptions (commodity, weight, dimensions, pickup and delivery details, hazards, appointment times) are accurate, that it is not a broker double-brokering a load without disclosure, and that no load is hazardous material, regulated waste, or contraband unless disclosed in writing and accepted by POTENT in writing before pickup.
Rate Confirmations and Rates

Rates are confirmed per load in writing (or through the POTENT platform) before work begins. POTENT keeps 100% of the agreed rate for the load. A confirmed rate may be adjusted only by a new written confirmation. Accessorial charges (detention, layover, redelivery, additional stops, lumper fees, tolls, extra labor, loading beyond described scope) are payable in addition when authorized in writing or caused by Dispatch Partner's inaccurate information or delay.
Payment Terms

Until POTENT completes account verification, payment is Prepay or Quick Pay. After verification, POTENT may extend terms of up to Net 7 days from the invoice date, never longer, at its discretion and revocable at any time. Late amounts bear 1.5% per month or the maximum permitted by law, whichever is less, and Dispatch Partner pays reasonable collection costs and attorneys' fees to the extent allowed by Georgia law. Dispatch Partner may not deduct or set off amounts without written agreement. Disputes about part of an invoice do not delay payment of the undisputed part.
Factoring and Assignment of Payment

If Dispatch Partner uses a factoring company, it must give POTENT a signed Notice of Assignment and remittance details. Payment to the party named in a valid notice discharges Dispatch Partner's obligation. POTENT may rely on remittance instructions confirmed by phone with a verified contact and is not liable for payment sent as instructed in a fraudulent change request that was not verified.
Performance of Services

POTENT controls the method, manner and means of performing its services, including equipment, drivers, helpers and route selection. POTENT may refuse a load that is unsafe, over weight, not as described, or that it cannot lawfully carry. POTENT does not guarantee pickup or delivery times unless they are confirmed in writing as time-critical, and will use commercially reasonable efforts to meet confirmed appointments.
Load Documentation, Photos and Proof of Delivery

POTENT will photograph freight at pickup and delivery, note visible condition and exceptions on the bill of lading, and provide a signed bill of lading and proof of delivery. Dispatch Partner will provide accurate load documents before pickup. A bill of lading signed without exception is evidence of delivery in good order.
Loading, Unloading and Detention

Unless agreed in writing, the shipper loads and the receiver unloads. Detention and layover are charged after two (2) hours free time at the rate confirmed, or if none, at the rate in POTENT's current rate card. Detention starts only after the two free hours have fully passed at that stop, and must be supported by timestamped messages or app events sent to the POTENT dispatch office. POTENT may document and charge for delays outside its control.
Weight, Capacity and Scope Changes

POTENT's truck has a maximum legal payload. Loads that exceed it, or that differ materially from the tender, may be refused, split into additional trips, or re-priced by a new written rate confirmation before work continues.
Receipts, Records and Right to Audit

Each party will keep records of loads for at least three (3) years. Dispatch Partner may audit records directly relevant to charges under this Agreement on reasonable written notice, during business hours, no more than once a year.
Waiver of Carrier's Lien

POTENT waives any lien rights against freight in its possession as security for payment of the freight charge, except where law requires otherwise or where Dispatch Partner's payment has failed on that load.
Insurance

POTENT maintains Auto Liability insurance of at least $750,000 per occurrence and Motor Truck Cargo insurance of at least $100,000 per occurrence, and will provide a certificate of insurance on request. Dispatch Partner will maintain the contingent cargo, general liability and surety bond or trust fund that apply to its own authority and provide evidence on request.
Loss, Damage and Delay

POTENT's liability for loss of or damage to freight is limited to the lesser of the actual loss and the amounts stated in the rate confirmation; if none are stated, the lesser of the actual value, $0.50 per pound or $100,000 per shipment, unless a higher value is declared in writing and accepted before pickup. POTENT is not liable for delay except where a time-critical service was confirmed in writing. Claims must be filed in writing within 48 hours of delivery with supporting documents; POTENT will acknowledge within 30 days and pay or decline within 120 days as federal rules require where they apply.
Indemnity

Each party will defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other from third-party claims, losses and reasonable costs to the extent caused by its own negligence, willful misconduct, breach of this Agreement, or violation of law. Dispatch Partner is solely responsible for the accuracy of the information it provides about each load.
Limitation of Liability

Except for payment obligations, indemnity for third-party bodily injury or property damage, fraud and willful misconduct, neither party is liable to the other for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, including lost profits or business.
Non-Circumvention and Sub-Contracting

POTENT will not subcontract or re-broker a load without Dispatch Partner's prior written consent. Dispatch Partner will not contact POTENT's shippers, receivers or drivers to solicit them for the same lane for twelve (12) months after a load, except where they were Dispatch Partner's own customers before the load.
Cargo Care and Liability

Dispatch Partner and its drivers are responsible for the safe transport, custody and care of cargo from the moment pickup is completed until a signed proof of delivery or bill of lading is obtained. Dispatch Partner will carry the cargo insurance POTENT requires for the load and will reimburse POTENT or the affected customer for the actual cash value of cargo lost, damaged or stolen while in its possession, except where caused by POTENT or the shipper.
Customer Non-Solicitation by Drivers and Carriers

During the term and for twelve (12) months after it ends for any reason, a driver, owner-operator or carrier working through POTENT will not directly or indirectly solicit, contract with or perform logistics, hauling, freight or junk-removal services for any POTENT customer it was introduced to, assigned or learned of through POTENT, without POTENT's prior written consent. Because a breach would cause harm that is hard to measure, POTENT may ask the courts in Rockdale County, Georgia for an injunction in addition to any other remedy, including lost profits from the circumvention. This section is limited to the extent Georgia's Restrictive Covenants Act requires.
Confidentiality and Data

Each party will protect the other's non-public business information (rates, customers, systems, load details) and use it only for performing this Agreement, except as required by law. Personal information is handled under POTENT's Privacy Policy. This section survives for three (3) years after termination.
Compliance, Safety and Anti-Fraud

Each party will follow applicable law, including FMCSA regulations that apply to it, sanctions and anti-corruption law, and will not engage in identity theft, cargo theft, fictitious pickups or fraudulent payment redirection. POTENT may delay or stop work when it reasonably suspects fraud or when a safety or legal issue arises.
Independent Contractors
The parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, employment or agency relationship, and neither may bind the other.
Assignment, Modification and Electronic Signature

Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other's written consent, except to a successor of substantially all its business on notice. It may be modified only in writing signed (including electronically under the E-SIGN Act) by both parties. POTENT keeps a record of the version, time and device used to accept it.
Governing Law and Dispute Resolution

Georgia law governs, and federal transportation law governs where it applies. The parties will first try to resolve a dispute by good-faith negotiation for 30 days, then by non-binding mediation if either asks, and then in the state or federal courts for Rockdale County, Georgia, which have exclusive jurisdiction. The prevailing party in a payment dispute may recover reasonable attorneys' fees to the extent allowed by law.
Notices, Severability, Waiver and Complete Agreement

Notices must be in writing to the contact information on file and are effective on delivery (email counts when receipt is confirmed or sent to the address on file). If a provision is unenforceable the rest remains in effect. Failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver. This Agreement and each signed rate confirmation are the entire agreement on their subject and replace prior discussions.

privacy: Who We Are and What This Covers

POTENT LOGISTICS LLC and POTENT OPERATIONS LLC ("POTENT," "we") provide delivery, junk removal and hauling services and the POTENT OS software platform. This policy explains what personal information we collect through our websites, apps, text messages, calls and services (the "Services"), how we use it, and your choices. It applies to customers who book with us, drivers and carriers, dispatch partners, and software customers and their staff. When a company that licenses POTENT OS uses it to serve its own customers, that company decides how that information is used, and we process it on its behalf.
Information We Collect

Contact and account details: name, phone, email, company, addresses, logins and password hashes. Job details: pickup and drop-off addresses, item descriptions, photos and videos you or our drivers take, notes, signatures, proof-of-delivery and bill-of-lading records, quotes, payments and invoices. Business verification: USDOT and MC numbers, EIN, insurance and bond documents, identification documents and selfies for driver and partner verification. Location: your address, and for drivers, device location while a job is active or while the app is open, used for dispatch, tracking and safety. Payments: processed by Stripe; we receive confirmations and limited card details (brand, last four digits), not full card numbers. Device and usage data: IP address, device and browser type, pages and actions, login times and approximate location from IP, cookies and similar technologies. Communications: messages, call recordings or notes, support requests. Terms acceptance records: the version accepted, time, and device and network address.
Precise Location

When you use our booking pages, ask for an automated route estimate, or track a dispatch vehicle, we may collect your device's precise location, with your permission. We use it only to check distance from our base, work out road miles and arrival times, and coordinate the job. You can turn location off in your device settings; booking by typing the address still works.
Job Photos and Property Documentation

Our drivers photograph the site and the load at pickup, during loading, and at delivery, disposal and completion. Photos carry timestamps and may carry location data. We use them to confirm the job was done, support billing, and resolve claims and chargebacks. Photos may show your property and belongings.
Identity Verification

To meet cargo, disposal and fraud-prevention requirements, we may ask to see, and may keep a copy of, government-issued ID (such as a driver's license) from a customer or authorized agent at pickup or delivery. We use it only to confirm authority to release or receive items and to protect both sides from unauthorized removal or illegal disposal. We do not sell it, and we keep it only as long as needed for those purposes and any claim.
How We Use Information

To give quotes, schedule, perform and document jobs; take payment and send receipts; send confirmations, arrival times and tracking links; verify partners and drivers and prevent fraud; keep records for claims and disputes; provide customer support; run, secure, debug and improve the Services; comply with law and enforce our terms; and, if you agree, send promotions. We may use photos and job records in anonymized or aggregated form to improve estimating tools, and we do not use your photos for advertising without your permission.
Texts and Calls

If you give us your mobile number, you agree we may text and call about your job and account. Message frequency varies with your job. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out of texts, HELP for help. Marketing texts are sent only with your separate consent, which is not a condition of buying anything.
Automated Tools and AI

Some tools use automated systems, including AI, to read documents, translate text, geocode addresses, and estimate load size and weight from photos. These produce estimates that our staff review before a quote is final. We do not use them to make decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on you without human review.
How We Share Information

With service providers that act for us under contract: hosting and database (Supabase, Netlify), payments (Stripe), email and messaging delivery, mapping and routing (OpenStreetMap, the U.S. Census Bureau geocoder), document and AI processing providers, and analytics. With our drivers, helpers, vendors and disposal facilities as needed to do your job. With a customer's or partner's own company when we act as its service provider. With insurers, claims administrators, factoring companies and professional advisers where needed. With authorities when required by law or to protect rights, safety and property. In a merger, financing or sale of our business. We do not sell personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising.
Cookies and Similar Technologies
We use essential storage to keep you signed in and remember settings, and limited analytics to understand site use. You can block cookies in your browser, but parts of the Services may not work.
How Long We Keep Information

We keep job and payment records for as long as needed for the job, for tax, insurance, claims and legal purposes (generally up to seven years), and verification documents only as long as needed for compliance. We delete or anonymize information we no longer need.
Security

We use access controls, encryption in transit, per-company data separation, role-based access and audit records. No system is perfectly secure. Keep your password confidential and tell us if you suspect unauthorized access.
Your Choices and Rights

You may ask to access, correct or delete your personal information, to receive a copy, or to opt out of marketing, by emailing potentlogistics@pm.me. Depending on where you live, you may have additional rights under state privacy laws, including the right to know, delete, correct and opt out of sale or sharing (we do not sell or share), and to appeal a denial. We will verify your request and respond within the time the law requires. We will not discriminate against you for using these rights. If you are a customer of a company using POTENT OS, contact that company first.
Children
The Services are not directed to people under 18 and we do not knowingly collect their information. If you believe a child has given us information, contact us and we will delete it.
Driver Location and Safety Data

Drivers who use our app agree that location is collected during active work and shared with dispatch, and with the customer for tracking links for that job. Drivers can see when tracking is on. We keep location history only as long as needed for job records, safety, payment disputes and legal requirements.
Changes to This Policy
We will post updates here with a new date, and tell you of material changes through the Services or by email. This version is effective October 8, 2026.
